visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat five-step contact wizards and generic 'get in touch' pages: one-screen V3Ask in the first viewport, a reach control with one dominant call door carrying a live hours state and the principal photograph, and the brokers who answer shown as photographs rather than a flat hairline list.

competitiveBrief.productLock: hero Call/text/write + address on fold + Call|Text|Email|Schedule PASS + form+SMS + brokers→/team; FAQ optional; do not reopen CTAs as missing
competitiveBrief.refuse: Five-step wizard. Four equal link cells. Looking that reopens Call|Text|Email|Schedule as missing. Invented reply-time.

beats.text: Hero H1 is Call, text, or write — one conversion sentence, not a five-step contact wizard.
Street address sits on the fold (115 NW Oregon Ave #2). A visitor can find the office without scrolling.
Call is on the reach control at display scale with live published hours. PASS regression — do not drop Call.
Text sits on the same reach control as Call. PASS regression — do not drop Text.
Email sits on the same reach control as Call and Text. PASS regression — do not drop Email.
Schedule sits on the same reach control as Call, Text, and Email. PASS regression — do not drop Schedule.
Form plus SMS consent (ContactAsk) is the write path. Do not reopen CTAs as missing when the form is present.
Brokers who answer door to /team. FAQ (V3Answers) is optional. Do not invent a reply-time clock.

note: SITE-96. Order is Breadcrumb, ContactFold (Quiet H1 + sourced Google-reviews figure, V3Doors #reach --lead Call at display scale with V3OnDuty published hours plus Text/Email/Schedule as the light door column, ContactAsk as the one ask, homepage-compact AboutFaces for who answers), V3Answers, Footer. Consent checkbox is padded to --v3-tap. Live state is published hours only. tasteReview scores and demoMatch are judge-written only.

requiredComponents.name: V3Breadcrumb
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. Home > Contact. Current page never a link.

requiredComponents.name: ContactFold
requiredComponents.section: SITE-80 first viewport: reach column (Quiet + V3Doors) beside the one ask. Do not open on four identical link rows.

requiredComponents.name: V3Quiet
requiredComponents.section: Opens the page. H1 is Call, text, or write (or the CMS title when it is not a bare Contact). One true line plus the sourced Google-reviews figure. Listing summary door when ?listingKey= is present.

requiredComponents.name: V3Doors
requiredComponents.section: #reach. One reach control, not four equal cells: `primary` on the call door (display scale, a larger bounding box than any other door) carrying the V3OnDuty live state and its trace; text, email and Schedule as lighter alternatives. A visitor who wants a human should not have to find a form field first, and should not meet four interchangeable boxes when they get there.

requiredComponents.name: ContactAsk
requiredComponents.section: One-screen V3Ask. Same submitContactForm fields as the old five-step sheet. SMS consent checkbox padded to 44px on this route. Consent copy is SMS_CONSENT_TEXT, untouched.

requiredComponents.name: V3Answers
requiredComponents.section: CONTACT_FAQ_ITEMS as native disclosures, remaining edges in the rail. splitQuietItems at the page so a leftover prose row cannot vanish.

requiredComponents.name: AboutFaces
requiredComponents.section: Who answers, headingLevel 2 — the same roster primitive /team and /about use, with the canonical broker cutouts and their reach chips. No record figures here: this route is dynamic and the per-broker MLS reads belong on the two cached pages.

requiredComponents.name: V3OnDuty
requiredComponents.section: The live state on the reach control: published booking hours against the Pacific clock, from crm_company_settings.booking_hours — the same rows /book offers time from. NEVER a reply-time figure (SITE-09, V3OnDuty.view.ts).

deferredComponents.name: V3Sheet
deferredComponents.reason: The five-step sheet was the problem this page left. Ask is the whole form at once.

deferredComponents.name: V3Stage
deferredComponents.reason: Contact is not a media page. The ask is the job.

deferredComponents.name: V3Proof
deferredComponents.reason: Reviews live on /reviews. A proof band here would restated that page.

deferredComponents.name: V3Ledger
deferredComponents.reason: The brokers band was a flat hairline row per broker with no visual encoding — the 2026-09-08 evaluator's own finding. AboutFaces does that job on every other page; a second, flatter way of listing the same three people is how one site becomes two (TASTE.md consistency).

removedComponents: Five-step V3Sheet contact wizard (Matt 2026-09-01: how they get hold of us must be simple).

ContactFold -- Quiet H1 + sourced reviews figure | reach control + ContactAsk in the first viewport
V3Quiet #contact -- H1 and the one true line (inside the fold)
V3Doors #reach -- Call at display scale with live published hours; Text, Email, Schedule as the light door column

tells: The stacked-section page. — mobile375.png first viewport is Quiet, then address, then Call / Text / Email / Schedule as repeating hairline rows, with the write path shoved off-screen.
Cream box. — error-open-desktop.png leaves Name / Email / Phone as idle navy pills; the beui error object is only a caption under an empty field, and the message textarea never grows a check.

defects.finding: At 375 the first screen is the H1, a reviews sentence, the office address, then four stacked reach rows; only the Talk to a broker eyebrow peeks. The write path and SMS consent are not in the first viewport, so the page's job is not one path from what a visitor actually sees.
Text, Email, and Schedule stack as equal hairline rows under Call. Desktop's display-scale Call with a lighter side column collapses into the four-row list the class was told not to open on.

success-open shows the beui check on Name, Email, and Phone. The message textarea in error-open and success-open is a static rounded box with a caption and no check, so the write path is two different field objects. error-open also never shows the shake or an error icon; empty pills plus Enter name is the still.

defects.section: Who answers vs sent-focus The brokers
defects.finding: hours-empty-open-desktop.png and sent-open-mobile375.png show three editorial cutouts. sent-focus-desktop.png still shows a gray hairline roster with 40px avatars, OR license numbers, and a cookie bar covering the last row — two roster forms for the same three people.
The full-page tour and sent captures still show four equal door cells (two phone tiles, email, Book a broker) and a gray broker ledger — the refused Looking form, not Call at display scale.

Shots cannot show the title tag or JSON-LD. Visible H1, address, and crawlable Call / Text / Email / Schedule doors are present, so SEO and page information look held, not risen. A prettier fold with SEO only held is a hold.

tasteReview.dullest: The 375 first viewport. Desktop's one idea — Call as a hero figure with the form beside it — dies on the small screen, and what remains is a stacked list of Text / Email / Schedule hairlines while the actual ask is somewhere below. The Send a message panel itself is every brokerage contact form shipped since 2014.
tasteReview.beats: Apple Support Contact (https://support.apple.com/contact) — we win on how easy it is to reach a named local broker: display-scale number, live published hours, 115 NW Oregon Ave #2 on the fold, and photographs of who answers. We do not win on first-viewport simplicity at 375, where Apple still puts one path in front of you.
tasteReview.verdict: This is a competent navy-and-cream contact fold, not a breathtaking one. demoMatch is true because success-open.png shows the beui-input check on the text fields, restyled navy on cream, and error-open.png shows the error line — the shake itself is invisible in a still, and the textarea never joins that object. competitiveBriefPass is true: Call, text, or write; the Bend office on the fold; Call at display scale with live hours; Text, Email, and Schedule on the same reach control; form plus SMS; Who answers with a Meet the team door. SEO and inventory look held from pixels (H1, sourced 5.0 from 25 Google reviews, live hours, address, the ask), not improved; JSON-LD cannot be certified from shots. The node is not Tip Ready on taste: the 375 stack, the leftover four-cell full-page captures, and the dual broker roster keep this in the 60s.
